  `popoverTarget` does not run again. It is not `stopPropagation()`ed, and other listeners
  (focus, hover, the consumer's pass-through handlers) are untouched;
- finds the part rendering **`aria-disabled="true"`** for as long as it renders `data-pending`
  (section 3.6).

The guard reads **only** a synchronous in-flight counter in `useActionTrigger` (so two
activations in one task are caught), never the last render's `pending`: after the action
settled, React may hold the commit that clears `pending` for as long as any other async action
is pending (entanglement, 2.3 item 5) or while the resulting render suspends, and a click in
that window starts a new run rather than being dropped (the review's probe showed a
rendered-`pending` guard losing two of three clicks on a non-awaiting action;
`design/components/button.md` 5.2). So `aria-disabled` may outlast the guard by the held window.
The one exception stays `Button`'s function `formAction`, whose only source is React's form
status, a render value (`button.md` 5.2).

**`"run"`**. Every activation starts a run in the part's own transition:

- the guard cancels nothing: each click also performs its default action (a link navigates, a
  `formAction` Button submits again, a command runs again). A part that cancels the click as
  its own mechanism (a Close part in library mode) keeps doing so; that is not the guard;
- **`data-pending` / `state.pending` only, no `aria-disabled`** from pending: the part still
  acts, and telling assistive technology it is unavailable would be false. `pending` stays true
  until every run has settled and the result has committed;
- **the continuation (a Close part's close, an item's menu close, a toast's close on settle)
  runs once, when the last run in flight settles, and only if the latest run resolved**: it is the latest run's continuation, still
  under that run's open-generation guard (3.4). So "a rejection leaves the overlay / menu /
  toast open" holds in both modes, and the part stays (pending) until its last run is done:
  library-mode and JS-free Close parts, a closing `Menu.Item` and a `Toast.Action` with
  `closeOnSettle` alike. An older run that resolves runs nothing; an older run that rejects
  after the latest resolved is reported and the close still runs when it settles.
  Implemented in `useActionTrigger` (3.4), so it applies to every part that passes `then`; the
  steps of the continuous controls pass none;
- errors follow 2.4 as for any owner: the **latest** run's
  rejection reaches the Error Boundary above the part, after every older run has settled; an
  **older** run's rejection is passed to `reportError`, each once. Since the part does not
  leave before its last run (the bullet above), the owner-left route (a rejection after the part left)
  is reached in `"run"` mode only when something else removes the part meanwhile (a dismissal,
  `toast.dismiss`), as in `"ignore"` mode. An ignored activation, by contrast, is not a run and
  reports nothing;
- a `Button` with a function `formAction` is React's form channel, not the library's
  transition: overlapping submissions behave as React's own submitter does, which includes
  React **dropping** the rejection of an older overlapping submission (verified on 19.3.1,
  `memo/architect/143-design-questions.md`). The library cannot observe that rejection and does
  not report it; the Button page says so and points to `whilePending="ignore"` and to
  `useActionState`.

**Not offered**: `"queue"`. Ordered, result-threaded runs are `useActionState`,
passed as `formAction` or called from the action. The related accepted point from the same
discussion: a set-valued action's `next` may contain still-pending changes (the set-valued
bullet above); documented, and `useActionState` is the answer there too.

"Await nothing" (`action={() => { void inc(); }}`) stays valid for "the UI must not wait" (2.3
item 5); it is not needed to make every click count, since a `Button` runs every activation by
default and a counter that wants pending state and error routing simply awaits.

### conventions.md 2.4, as it stood before the second pass

### 2.4 Errors

An action that throws or rejects reaches the **nearest Error Boundary above the library
component that owns the transition** (the `Root`, or the component itself), with two exceptions,
both rejections React itself would drop, which are passed to the global `reportError` instead:
the rejection of a **superseded** action (an older one, when a newer action of the same owner was
dispatched before it settled), and the rejection of the latest action when its **owner is gone**
(unmounted, or hidden by `<Activity>`) by the time it arrives. The library never swallows
an error. There is no `errorAction` prop in v0.

Why the exception. `useTransition` stores one thenable per `startTransition` call as a state
update and only the newest is ever unwrapped, so React drops an older action's rejection
entirely: no boundary, no `reportError`, no `unhandledrejection` (verified on 19.3.1, both
resolution orders, both modes; `memo/architect/143-design-questions.md`). Throwing it from
render instead would replace the whole UI because of an intent the user had already replaced,
a behaviour React does not have for the same code written by hand. So the library does what
React's standalone `startTransition` does with a rejection it has no boundary for: it reports
it. The UI stays up and shows the latest intent; the failure reaches `window.onerror`,
monitoring tools and test runners.

Contract:

- The **latest** dispatch's rejection propagates through React's own path while its owner is
  mounted and visible (not hidden by `<Activity>`, `keepMounted` or a Suspense fallback): the
  hook rethrows it inside the transition. It reaches the boundary only **after every older
  overlapping dispatch has settled**: React holds the boundary's commit while the entangled
  action lane is still pending (section 2.3 item 5). React behaviour, documented so a test that
  rejects the newest of two dispatches does not expect the fallback before the older one
  resolves.
- "Latest" is judged **when the rejection arrives**: a dispatch is superseded when another
  dispatch of the same hook instance was made after it, whether that one is still pending or has
  already settled.
- A **superseded** dispatch's rejection is caught by the hook and passed to `reportDropped`
  (`internal/report-dropped.ts`): the global `reportError` (a window `error` event), or
  `console.error` in an environment without it. Nothing is thrown, no state is written, no
  boundary is involved, and the newer dispatch's outcome is unaffected.
- **Every** superseded rejection of a burst is reported, each once, in the order they arrive.
  When the latest dispatch rejects as well, it still goes to the boundary; the two routes are
  independent.
- Reports **continue after unmount**: a superseded action that rejects after its component left
  is still reported.
- **The latest rejection once the owner is gone is reported too**. The hook rethrows a
  latest rejection only while its component's effects are connected (`useConnected` in
  `use-connected.ts`: set in a mount layout effect, cleared by its cleanup); otherwise it passes
  it to `reportDropped` and returns. Why: React routes a transition's rejection only through a
  render of the component that owns it; with that component unmounted nothing reads it (probed
  on 19.3.1 with `useActionTrigger`: no boundary, no `reportError`, no
  `unhandledrejection`). Effect cleanup also runs when the component is **hidden**: by an
  `<Activity mode="hidden">` (the consumer's, or the library's own: a closed overlay with
  `keepMounted`, `internal/overlay-popup.tsx`), or by a shown Suspense boundary that re-suspends
  and shows its fallback (probed; Toast's Suspense guard around the Root's content is one). A
  rejection that arrives while hidden is reported as well and does **not** reach the boundary
  when the component is shown again, where React would deliver it: a deliberate deviation from
  React. Each rejection goes one route, exactly
  once. Reachable: a `Toast.Action` whose toast is closed while its action runs (toast.md
  walkthrough 6) or whose content an urgent `toast.update` made suspend; a `Menu.Item`, menu
  checkable item or Close part whose overlay is dismissed meanwhile, unmounting it or (with
  `keepMounted`) hiding it (menu.md walkthrough 4); any state owner removed while its action is
  pending. Not covered, React behaviour: a latest rejection that arrives while the owner is
  connected is rethrown, and if the owner unmounts in the same commit, before React renders it
  again, React still drops it (a tiny window; not handled).
- A consumer who catches inside the action is unaffected, as before.
- **A request superseded by a fact**: a fact on an overlay Root (`adoptFact`, 3.4)
  makes every dispatch in flight superseded at once, so a later rejection of one of them is
  passed to `reportDropped`, as for any superseded dispatch, and its resolution commits
  nothing.
- **A fact handler's errors are not action errors**: an `on*` handler's synchronous throw and
  its returned promise's rejection go to `reportError` (the handler rule of 2.1,
  `internal/call-urgent-handler.ts`); nothing reaches an Error Boundary, and the library's own
  bookkeeping around the call (the committed `false` of a fact, a toast's queue write, a
  Combobox text write) stands.
- Both hooks (`useControllableAction`, `useActionTrigger`) do this themselves, per instance, and
  so does `Form.Root` for the submissions it runs in its own transition. A
  component with **two transition channels** (Slider and NumberField: steps through
  `useActionTrigger`, commits through `useControllableAction`) needs nothing extra: each channel
  judges "latest" among its own runs and reports its own superseded rejections, also while the
  other channel's action is pending. There is no hook-order constraint and no shared capture
  (`captureSuperseded` is removed).
- For a **pure trigger** the superseded path is reachable exactly when its `whilePending` is
  `"run"` (section 2.5.1; the default of `Button`): its runs overlap and the rules above
  apply to them as to any owner. With `"ignore"` it never has two runs in flight, so every
  rejection is a latest one.

Consequence for tests: in a real browser `reportError` dispatches a window `error` event, which
vitest browser mode counts as an unhandled error, and vitest's jsdom environment has no
`reportError` (the `console.error` fallback runs). A test that makes an older action reject stubs
the global (`vi.stubGlobal("reportError", vi.fn())`) and asserts on it (section 10.1).

Optimistic state reverts automatically. Uncontrolled committed state is written only after the
action resolves, so a rejected action leaves it untouched (section 3.3). A controlled parent gets
the same by updating its state on success only.

A consumer who wants inline error UI instead of a boundary catches inside the action. Note that a
caught error makes the action *resolve*, which the library treats as success:

```tsx
<Toggle
  pressed={favorite}
  pressedChangeAction={async (next) => {
    try {
      await api.setFavorite(id, next);
      startTransition(() => setFavorite(next));
    } catch (e) {
      startTransition(() => setError(e)); // `favorite` unchanged, optimistic reverts
    }
  }}
/>
```

In uncontrolled mode a swallowed error therefore commits the new value. Use controlled mode when
the parent needs to veto.

### conventions.md 1.2, the `type` and `disabled` bullet, as it stood before the second pass

- Element-type-specific attributes are set only when they apply to the rendered element:
  `type="button"` is emitted for a `<button>` and omitted for `render={<a href />}` or any other
  **host** element, rather than landing as a meaningless attribute on an anchor. A **component**
  `render` element (`render={<MyButton />}`) receives `type` too: the part
  cannot see what it renders, a missing `type` on a component that renders a `<button>` inside a
  form is a silent submit, and an ignored `type` on one that renders a link is harmless. The
  shared predicate is `rendersButton(render)` (`internal/render-element.ts`): `true` for no
  `render`, the function form, a host `"button"` and any component element. For `disabled`
  the choice depends on who acts on the click. **Native `disabled`** on a host `<button>` (no
  `render`, the function form), and wherever the click's effect is the **browser's own** (a
  submit, a reset, a JS-free invoker command) and the element **may be a button** (a host
  `<button>` / `<input>`, or a component): only native `disabled` stops a submission or a
  command before hydration and blocks implicit submission, and if a component turns out to
  render a link the part fails at its job either way. **`aria-disabled="true"` with a cancelled
  click** only in three cases: the element certainly cannot be natively disabled (a host `<a>`,
  `<div>`; native `disabled` means nothing there and would expose an enabled link to assistive
  technology); the part's **own click handler is the action** and the element is not certainly
  a host `<button>` (a link or component render); or the consumer **opts into** a focusable
  disabled control (APG: a `Button` inside a Toolbar or with `focusableWhenDisabled`, a menu
  item). The handler is what makes `aria-disabled` safe (it returns before dispatch and
  `preventDefault()`s), so the browser-run parts (`Form.Submit`; a JS-free command Trigger /
  Close; a `Button` whose `type` is `"submit"` / `"reset"`, by default with `formAction`, or
  that carries `commandfor` / `popoverTarget`, with or without `action`: the browser acts on
  that click too) keep native `disabled` on any element that may be a button. The parts whose
  handler is all the click does (`Button` with `action` and none of those, Toggle,
  ToggleGroup.Item, Menu.Trigger, Combobox.Trigger / Clear, NumberField.Increment / Decrement,
  Toast.Action / Close, and the Close and Trigger parts of Dialog and Popover in the modes
  where they handle the click; `design/components/button.md` 17.1) take the `aria-disabled`
  branch on a link or component render. A part with no click handler of its own (`Form.Submit`,
  a JS-free command Trigger / Close) that lands in the `aria-disabled` branch on a host link
  installs one while disabled that only cancels the click (`cancelClick`), so a disabled link
  never navigates after hydration; before hydration nothing stops a link. When `disabled` and a pending pure trigger's
  `aria-disabled` (3.6) meet on a natively disabled element, native `disabled` wins and no
  `aria-disabled` is rendered. In that `aria-disabled` branch an **invoker also
  owns its invoker attributes (`popoverTarget`, `commandfor`, `command`) as `undefined`**: `aria-disabled` has no
  behaviour, and a disabled component render spreading onto a real `<button commandfor
  command>` would otherwise be a live invoker in the server HTML before hydration. The part owns
  `aria-disabled` only where it computes it (that branch, or a pending pure trigger); on a host
  button outside it the consumer's own `aria-disabled` passes through. When the element is
  unknown, each attribute takes the choice that is harmless if the guess is wrong.
  One helper implements the rule for every such part, `Button` and `Form.Submit` included:
  `disabledButton(render, disabled, { handlesClick?, alwaysFocusable? })` in
  `internal/render-element.ts` returns `props`, the owned `disabled` / `aria-disabled` keys of
  the branch it chose, and `invoker`, whether `commandfor` / `command` may render;
  `handlesClick: false` is the browser-run case above (native unless the element certainly
  cannot be disabled) and `alwaysFocusable` the opt-in focusable case (`SubmenuTrigger` through
  `usePopoverTrigger`'s `submenuItem`, `Button`'s Toolbar and `focusableWhenDisabled`).
  `pendingAriaDisabled` in the same module merges the branch with a pure trigger's pending
  `aria-disabled`.

### conventions.md 1.1, the part vocabulary table, as it stood before the second pass

Part vocabulary (reuse these names; invent a new one only when none fits):

| Part | Meaning | Default element |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Root` | Owns state, context and the transition. May render no DOM (overlays) or a wrapper; a Root that owns a form value but no visible element may render exactly one `<input type="hidden">` when `name` is given (Combobox); a Form's Root is the `<form>` itself; NumberField's is a `div[role=group]`. | `div` / `form` or none |
| `List` | Groups triggers; owns keyboard navigation between them. In Combobox it is the ARIA `listbox` inside the `Popup` (the Popup is the container, because a listbox may contain only options and groups). | `div` |
| `Item` | One entry in a multi-item component (Accordion, Menu). Menu's is a `button[role=menuitem]` with an `action`; ToggleGroup's is a `button[aria-pressed]`, the Toggle element, whose pressed state is the Root's. | `div` / `details` / `button` |
| `Trigger` / `Tab` | The interactive element the user acts on. | `button` |
| `ContextTrigger` | A region whose `contextmenu` (right-click, Ctrl+click, Shift+F10 / the ContextMenu key at a focused descendant, a library long-press for touch) opens the owner's `Popup` at the pointer (Menu). A plain element with **no role and no ARIA** (`aria-haspopup` is not allowed on generic roles and ARIA has no attribute for "has a context menu"); `data-open` / `data-pending` / `data-disabled`. May share a Root with a `Trigger` (a "More" button and a right-click region opening one popup). | `div` |
| `Panel` | Content region whose visibility is driven by library state (Tabs, Accordion). | `div` |
| `Popup` | Content that lives in the top layer (Tooltip, Popover, Menu). | `div[popover]` (Tooltip, Menu) or `dialog[popover]` (Popover) |
| `Indicator` | Purely visual element that tracks state (active tab marker; the fill of a Slider, placed by the consumer's CSS from the Root's `--slider-start` / `--slider-end`; the fill of a Progress / Meter, sized by the consumer's CSS from the Root's `--progress-value` / `--meter-value`). | `span` |
| `Label` | Names the owner. For `<fieldset>`-based groups (RadioGroup, CheckboxGroup) it renders `<legend>` and must be the Root's first child; for a component whose owner surface is an `Input` part (Combobox) it renders `<label for>`; for Slider it renders `label[for]` naming the only Thumb's input, or `label[id]` naming a multi-thumb Root (`role="group"`); for Field it renders `label[for]` naming the field's control, or `label[id]` that a group control (a `<fieldset>` Root) is `aria-labelledby` (the `for` is dropped once such a control registers); for NumberField it renders `label[for]` naming the visible input and its id names the Root group; for an output role that is not labelable (Progress, Meter) it renders `span[id]` and the Root references the id through `aria-labelledby` unconditionally, dangling when no Label is rendered. | `label` / `legend` / `span` |
| `Input` | The text field of a combobox-like component: `input[role=combobox]`, the owner's surface for `data-pending`, with the urgent `inputValue` state (section 2.6); or the visible text field of a NumberField (`input[type=text][inputmode]`, the owner surface for `data-pending`, with the urgent draft text), which renders the hidden native number input right after it. | `input` |
| `Parent` | A mixed-state checkbox that controls a subset of a CheckboxGroup (`values`): its checked/mixed state is derived from the group's optimistic set and its click dispatches for the whole subset. Never submitted (no `name`). | `input[type=checkbox]` |
| `Option` | One choice in a native `<select>` (Select; renders optimistic `data-selected`, equal to the platform's `:checked`) or in a listbox (Combobox: `div[role=option]`, never focused, `data-active` for virtual focus). | `option` / `div` |
| `Clear` | A `tabindex="-1"` button that empties a text field and dispatches the empty selection (Combobox). | `button` |
| `Empty` | Content the **library** shows only when a list has no mounted options and its results are neither stale nor loading (Combobox). | `div` |
| `Status` | A loading fallback or hint inside a popup (Combobox). Outside the `List` it is `role="status"`; **inside** the `List` it is the Suspense fallback, renders `role="none"` (a listbox may own only options and groups) and marks the list as loading: `aria-busy="true"` on the listbox, `Empty` hidden, nothing announced. | `div` |
| `Value` | The element that shows the current value. Select: the element the browser fills with the selected option's content; it has **no `children` prop**, since the parser and the browser write its content, so the part renders it with the hydration pattern of section 7.4. Slider: a `span` rendering the shown value (`children(state)`, or one thumb's value by `index`). Progress / Meter: a `span`, `aria-hidden` by default (the same text is in `aria-valuetext`), showing `formattedValue`. | `selectedcontent` / `span` |
| `Track` | The rail a slider's thumbs move along; owns pointer interaction (a press moves the nearest thumb) and is the geometry reference for pointer math. For Progress / Meter: the rail of the bar, with no interaction. | `div` |
| `Thumb` | A draggable value handle (Slider, one per value, explicit `index`): a styled element **containing** a visually hidden native `<input type="range">`, which is the focusable, labelled, form-participating `slider`. | `span` + `input[type=range]` |
| `Increment` / `Decrement` | `button[type=button][tabindex=-1]` that steps a numeric value, with press-and-hold (NumberField); `aria-controls` → the field's input; natively `disabled` when the next step would change nothing. | `button` |
| `Form` | A form whose successful submission completes the component's interaction (Dialog). | `form` |
| `Control` | The native form control a Field labels and describes: an `input`, or a `textarea` / `select` through `render`; must stay a native control. Any FUNSTACK form control inside a `Field.Root` plays the same role through `useFieldControl` (section 3.8). | `input` |
| `Description` | Describes the owner through `aria-describedby`: a `p[id]` the control (Field) or the `<dialog>` (Dialog) always references, mounted or not (a dangling reference is skipped). | `p` |
| `Error` | The message for a Field's current constraint violation: `div[id]`, rendered only while an error is shown, referenced through `aria-describedby` while it is; no live region, no `role`. | `div` |
| `Submit` | A form's submit button with the form channel's `data-pending` (`useFormStatus`). | `button[type=submit]` |
| `GroupLabel` | Names a `Group` (or a `RadioGroup` in Menu): an element with an id the group references through `aria-labelledby`. Not `Label`, which names the component's owner. | `div` |
| `Button` | A pure-trigger `button` with a bare `action` and its own `data-pending` (`useActionTrigger`). The general one is the single-element `Button` (`@funstack/ui/button`): `type="button"` by default (`"submit"` with `formAction`), runs every activation by default and, with `whilePending="ignore"`, ignores activation while its own action is pending (`aria-disabled="true"` meanwhile; 2.5.1), and reads `ToolbarContext` so that inside a Toolbar `disabled` renders `aria-disabled` and keeps the button focusable, as the APG Toolbar example wants. A Toolbar's command button is a `Button`; the Toolbar has no button part. | `button` |
| `Header`, `Group`, `Separator`, `Arrow` | Structural or decorative. `Separator` is an `<hr>` by default (implicit `separator` role); inside a Toolbar it carries `aria-orientation` perpendicular to the toolbar's (`Toolbar.Separator`). | as named |

## 2026-11-26, #163: Collapsible designed (proposed)

Architect, wave 23 (#162). New document `design/components/collapsible.md`, status proposed;
not implemented, and not yet accepted by the user. No conventions rule changed. Notes:
`memo/architect/collapsible-notes.md`.

What the design decides, and why:

- **`<details>` base, three parts.** `Collapsible.Root` is the `<details>` and the state owner,
  `Trigger` the `<summary>`, `Panel` a `div`. No wrapper `div` as in Accordion: a single
  disclosure has no set and no arrow keys. Cost, stated in the document: the Trigger must be the
  first child of the Root, so the Radix shape "trigger anywhere inside the Root" (a header row
  with other controls, a "show more" button under the content) is not available; an outside
  control uses controlled `open`. A second base (`button[aria-expanded]` plus a
  `hidden="until-found"` region, the Tabs machinery) was not designed: #163 asks for the
  `<details>` base, and two bases would be two components under one name.
- **`open` / `defaultOpen` / `openChangeAction`, no `onOpenChange`.** #163 names
  "`openAction` / `onOpenChange`"; the conventions' name for the request is `openChangeAction`
  (2.1), and the pair with `onOpenChange` exists only on overlay Roots, for a change the library
  cannot hold. A `<details>` has none: the click is intercepted, and what the browser does by
  itself (find-in-page, a click before hydration) is rolled back cheaply, which is why Accordion
  already treats it as a request with `reason: "platform"`. So conventions 3.9 does not apply
  and the `on*` allow-list is unchanged.
- **`defaultOpen` selects library mode.** Mode selection is conventions 3.9.11 without
  `onOpenChange`: JS-free when the Root has none of `open`, `defaultOpen`, `openChangeAction`.
  This differs from `Accordion.Item`, where `defaultOpen` is the JS-free spelling. Reason: the
  Root is the element and the owner at once, and with `defaultOpen` kept JS-free there is no
  uncontrolled library mode without an action (Accordion's `defaultValue={[]}`), which lazy
  Panel content needs. The HTML and the behaviour before hydration are the same either way.
- **Single-valued state, no reducer**, latest dispatch wins, as Toggle. `pending` on Root and
  Trigger is the Root's transition (the owner rule of 4.3), not Accordion's per-item
  "optimistic differs from committed".
- **Transition types** `fsui-collapsible`, `fsui-collapsible-expand`,
  `fsui-collapsible-collapse`: Accordion's change names, not the overlays' `open` / `close`.
- **`experimental_interpolateSize` on the Root**, which is the `<details>` itself here;
  `::details-content` inherits from its originating element.

To do when the design is accepted and implemented (registry rows, not rule changes):

- conventions 1.1, part vocabulary: `Root` may be the `<details>` itself (Collapsible).
- conventions 3.5 (the browser-owned examples), 3.7 (no `keepMounted`), 5.3 (the types row),
  7.3 (Collapsible next to Accordion) and 8 (`experimental_interpolateSize` on
  `Collapsible.Root`).
- `design/internal-hooks.md`: the index line of whatever is extracted (below).

Sharing with Accordion (a plan for the developer, not a rule):

- `Accordion.Trigger`'s click rule (the nested-interactive selectors, `preventDefault`, the
  disabled branch) and the `<details>` / `<summary>` element checks move to one flat module in
  `internal/`, used by both Triggers.
- The state side is not shared: Accordion's Root owns a set, reconciles all items in one mount
  dispatch and re-applies per item; Collapsible's Root is one `useControllableAction` over a
  boolean with one `toggle` handler, one mount reconciliation and one re-apply effect. Building
  Collapsible as a one-item exclusive Accordion was rejected: it brings the trigger registry,
  the arrow keys, the set machinery and a wrapper `div`.
- `Accordion.Item` outside any Root already works as a JS-free disclosure; whether it stays
  documented is open.

Test plan (conventions 10.1; jsdom unless noted):

- Roles and ARIA: `details` / `summary` / `div`; no `aria-expanded`; `aria-disabled` when
  disabled; element-check warnings for a wrong `render` element.
- Keyboard: Enter and Space (browser test: real engines synthesize the click; jsdom does not).
- Sync action, async action, rejection, superseded rejection, overlap (open then close, both
  orders of settling), post-await rule, controlled / uncontrolled parity: the Toggle rows on
  `open`, asserting `data-open` / `data-pending` on Root and Trigger, and the `open` attribute
  and Panel state on commit.
- Suspending content: the Panel's function form; the `<details>` stays closed and pending.
- Platform path: mount reconciliation (`renderToString`, set `open` before `hydrateRoot`, one
  dispatch with `reason: "platform"` and no event, StrictMode still one); `toggle` from
  `setAttribute("open", "")` dispatches with the event; a refused or rejected reveal is closed
  again; a reveal equal to the intended value does not dispatch; a disabled Root does not
  dispatch and is re-closed.
- Mode: none of the three props renders no handler and no `data-open`; `defaultOpen={false}`
  is library mode; switching modes warns; `transition` in JS-free mode warns.
- Function props and `render` element; the Directive row (three client files).
- Browser: `experimental_interpolateSize` (computed `interpolate-size` on the `<details>`),
  the `::details-content` transition, and one `transition` run with the types. Find-in-page is
  not scriptable.

## 2026-11-26, #163: Collapsible decided and implemented

Developer, wave 23 (#162). `design/components/collapsible.md` status proposed -> decided. The
user accepted the four recommendations of the design handback (issue comment, 2026-11-26):

1. `defaultOpen` selects library mode (design 2.1), `defaultOpen={false}` included.
2. `openChangeAction` only, no `onOpenChange` (design 2.2): the `on*` allow-list of conventions
   2.1 is unchanged, and the action-naming guard (`__tests__/action-naming.test.ts`) lists the
   three Collapsible Props types.
3. `<details>` is the only base; the Trigger must be the first child of the Root.
4. A standalone `Accordion.Item` (no Root) keeps working as a JS-free disclosure; the docs point
   to Collapsible for one disclosure. Recorded as a rule in `accordion.md` section 1.

Implementation: `packages/ui/src/collapsible/` (context, Root, Trigger, Panel; all `"use
client"`), subpath `@funstack/ui/collapsible`, root re-export. Sharing with Accordion as
planned: the Trigger click rule (nested interactive content, `preventDefault`) and the
`<details>` / `<summary>` element checks moved to `internal/details-summary.ts` (flat, a client
module because the checks are hooks); `Accordion.Item` and `Accordion.Trigger` use it, with
their messages unchanged (the part name is a parameter). The state side is not shared.

Registry rows added (no rule changed): conventions 1.1 (`Root` may be the `<details>`, `Panel`
lists Collapsible), 2.5 (single-valued list), 3.5 (examples), 3.7 (no `keepMounted`), 4.1 (the
`open` row), 5.3 (the types row), 7.3 (Collapsible next to Accordion), 8 (the
`experimental_interpolateSize` row); `internal-hooks.md` 3.4 (no reducer) and the file index.

Notes from the implementation (memo/developer/issue-163.md):

- The `toggle` handler treats `details.open === committed` as the library's own echo, as the
  design says. Consequence: while a close is pending (committed still open), a browser that
  closes and then re-opens the `<details>` is not dispatched; the close then commits. Accordion
  has the same rule.
- `::details-content` transitions are not listed by `getAnimations()` in Chromium, and in
  Firefox an `opacity` transition on `::details-content` does not run while the
  `grid-template-rows` one does. The browser row observes the box height instead.

## 2026-11-26, #163: Collapsible review fixes

Developer, after the review of `feat/163-collapsible` (memo/reviewer/review-163.md on branch
`review/163`). Wording only; no behaviour changed.

- Design 2.2, the re-apply bullet: a refused reveal is closed again; a rejection of the latest
  dispatch goes to the Error Boundary (the Root is replaced, so nothing is "closed again"); a
  superseded rejection goes to `reportError` and the DOM follows the later dispatch. The earlier
  text said a rejecting action closes the reveal again. A jsdom row covers the superseded case.
- Design 3.1, the `defaultOpen` row: default "none (JS-free mode)"; library mode without it
  starts as `false`.
- `useDetailsCheck` (`internal/details-summary.ts`) takes the platform semantics to name in its
  message: Accordion keeps "toggle, find-in-page, exclusive groups", Collapsible says "toggle,
  find-in-page, ::details-content" (it owns `name` and has no exclusive group).
- Not changed: the echo rule (review finding 3) is left for a separate issue.

## 2026-11-26, #164: Combobox `multiple` with chips (proposed)

Design for GitHub issue #164 (part of #162, wave 23). **Proposed**: written by the architect,
not yet accepted by the user and not implemented. The open decisions are listed at the end;
working notes in `memo/architect/combobox-multiple-notes.md`.

Sections changed:

- combobox.md: new section 15 (the whole design of `multiple`); decisions table row 2 (the
  chip parts and the hidden inputs), row 14 (no longer lists `multiple`), new row 16; 3.1 (the
  props shown are the single variant of a union); 9 (`aria-multiselectable`); 13 (the
  `multiple` item is replaced by what stays out: delimiters, a maximum, reordering, a disabled
  chip, an overflow part); the Status line.
- conventions.md 1.1: a second exception to "each part renders at most one DOM element", the
  hidden inputs of a Combobox Root (one per value with `multiple`). This is the one rule that
  changes. 2.5 (the list of set-valued owners names Combobox with `multiple`), 5.3 (the
  Combobox row: `fsui-combobox-deselect`) and 11 (the removal announcement) are additions to
  lists, not new rules.

The reasoning worth keeping:

- **Single mode is untouched.** `multiple: true` selects a second variant of the Root's props
  union (the `exclusive` pattern of ToggleGroup and Accordion with the default the other way
  round, because single selection shipped first). The mode is fixed at mount.
- **The text changes meaning, not shape.** In single mode the text is the selection's label,
  so the library writes it on a pick and rolls it back on a rejection. With `multiple` the
  text is only a search: a pick clears it and nothing ever rolls it back. That removes the
  per-dispatch text record and the "close in the commit that ends the action" path from the
  multiple mode instead of adding to them.
- **Set-valued rules apply as written** (conventions 2.2, 2.5, 3.3): `added` / `removed`, the
  patch reducer, the replay of resolved changes, the absolute form reset. The one difference
  from CheckboxGroup is order: pick order (the value's own order), because most options are
  not mounted and document order means nothing.
- **Chips render optimistic state**, so a removed chip disappears at once and a chip can only
  be pending while it is being added. Considered and not chosen: rendering the union of the
  optimistic and committed values so that a chip being removed stays with `data-pending`.
- **`Chips` is a list, not the field box** (Base UI's `Chips` wraps the Input). A `list` may
  not own a textbox, and without a list a screen reader has no "2 items".
- **Chip labels.** The library derives no label from a value, and with an async search the
  consumer may hold nothing but the value. `Chip`'s state therefore carries `label` from the
  label cache (2.3), which is written at the pick.
- **Real focus on chips, one Tab stop** (Base UI's model). Rejected: React Aria's separate
  grid (a second Tab stop and two more roles), Ark `TagsInput`'s highlight without focus
  (silent for a screen reader), and Backspace-only (no keyboard path to a chip that is not
  the last one except through the listbox).
- **`required` is computed** on the Input (conventions 3.6, CheckboxGroup 7): rendered only
  while the optimistic value is empty. A `required` on the Root was not chosen: the Input is
  where it is in single mode and where the browser shows the message. Unmatched text must not
  satisfy it, which is why focus leaving and Enter in a closed combobox clear the text.
- **One hidden input per value** rather than one hidden `<select multiple>`: a hidden select
  would be one element and post natively, but Firefox restores a select's state on reload and
  its reset algorithm would run against `selected` attributes React does not keep in step.
  While the selection is empty one nameless hidden input keeps a form-associated element for
  the reset listener and the Field.
- **A press on `ChipRemove` while the listbox is open closes it** (light dismiss, as `Clear`).
  Capturing the pointer to the Popup, the Input's trick, would retarget the click away from
  the button.

Open decisions for the user (recommendation first):

1. The text after a pick: cleared / kept / a prop.
2. The listbox after a pick: stays open / closes / a `closeOnSelect`-style prop.
3. Chip keyboard: real focus with arrows, Backspace and Delete / Backspace on the empty
   input only.
4. A chip whose removal is pending: disappears at once / stays with `data-pending`.
5. `allowCustomValue` text when focus leaves: added as a value / discarded.
6. The built-in English removal announcement (`announceRemoved`): ship it / no announcement.

To verify in a browser at implementation: focusing the Input in a chip's `keydown` delivers the
character to the Input in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit; screen readers announce the
`aria-selected` change of the active option in a multiselectable listbox (NVDA, JAWS,
VoiceOver), else the toggle needs an announcement too; a focusable `listitem` is read with its
position.

## 2026-11-26, #164: Combobox `multiple` decided and implemented

The user accepted the six recommendations of the entry above (issue comment, 2026-11-26):

1. The text is **cleared** after a pick.
2. The listbox **stays open** after a pick.
3. Chips take **real focus**, with one Tab stop (the Input).
4. A chip whose removal is pending **disappears at once** and comes back on rejection.
5. `allowCustomValue` text is **added as a value** when focus leaves.
6. `announceRemoved` **ships** (default English `"Japan removed"`).

combobox.md section 15 is now "decided"; the Status line no longer excludes it. No rule of
section 15 changed with the decisions: the section was written with the recommendations.

Amendments made at implementation (combobox.md 15.1, 15.2, 15.6):

- `Combobox.Chips` owns `onFocus` / `onBlur` as well (added to the `Omit` of
  `ComboboxChipsProps`): focus arriving on a chip closes the listbox and starts the press watch
  of the leave rule, and focus leaving a chip for outside the combobox is focus leaving. The
  Input owns the same pair for the same reason (3.2); `onFocusCapture` / `onBlurCapture` pass
  through.
- `Chips` renders `aria-labelledby` only while it has the `list` role (not empty): a role-less
  `div` may not be named.
- Escape on a chip is prevented as it moves focus to the Input, so the close request of an
  enclosing Dialog or Popover does not run (verified in Chromium and Firefox, browser row
  "Escape on a chip inside a modal Dialog").

Implementation notes (not rules):

- The Root keeps one component: both selection hooks are called on every render, the one for
  the other mode idle (no props, no action). The multiple one is
  `packages/ui/src/combobox/use-multiple-selection.ts` (the patch reducer, `change`, the whole
  form reset with the #151 rule of CheckboxGroup); Option, Chip and ChipRemove read
  `isSelected` / `isPending` from the context, so they do not branch on the mode.
- Chip labels are render state: a snapshot map written in the pick's event (before the
  dispatch, so the chip's first render has the label), when an Option for a selected value
  registers, and in a layout effect when values arrive from outside. The cache itself stays a
  ref map read by handlers only.
- `useComboboxForm` takes `resetValue(event)`; the Root computes the reset target per mode.
  `useDeferredLeave` takes `chipsRef` as a third inside region.
- Tests: the shared value-action suite runs against `Combobox.Root multiple` (driver
  `packages/ui/src/__tests__/drivers/combobox-multiple.tsx`, including the transition-type rows
  in `packages/ui/src/combobox/combobox-multiple-transition-types.test.tsx`);
  `packages/ui/src/combobox/combobox-multiple.test.tsx` (jsdom) and
  `packages/ui/src/combobox/combobox-multiple.browser.test.tsx`.

The points left to verify by the entry above:

- **A printable key on a chip lands in the Input** (the Input focused in the chip's `keydown`):
  verified with the real keyboard in Chromium 156 and Firefox 157 (a letter, a shifted letter,
  a digit); WebKit through CI (`workflow_dispatch` on the work branch), WebKit cannot run on the
  development machine.
- **Screen readers and the `aria-selected` change** of the active option in a multiselectable
  listbox: not verifiable in the automated suite. Chromium's accessibility tree (CDP) exposes
  `multiselectable` on the listbox and `selected` on each option, toggled by a pick. The NVDA,
  JAWS and VoiceOver pass is still to be done by hand; until it is, no extra announcement for a
  toggle.
- **A focusable `listitem` read with its position**: Chromium's tree exposes the chips as a
  list named by the Label with `focusable` list items; CDP shows no `posinset` / `setsize` for
  them (Chromium computes the position in the platform layer), so what a screen reader speaks
  is part of the same manual pass.

## 2026-11-26, #164: Combobox `multiple`, review amendments

From the review of the implementation (`memo/reviewer/review-164.md` on `review/164`); m1 is a
product-owner decision. Sections changed: combobox.md 15.6, 15.7; conventions 1.1 (wording).

- **M1, the removal announcement's text fallback (15.7).** It was the chip's `textContent`,
  which reads an `aria-hidden` "×" (the docs example announced "TypeScript× removed"). It is now
  the chip's text nodes, skipping `[aria-hidden="true"]` subtrees and the `ChipRemove` (whose
  elements register with the Root), whitespace collapsed and trimmed. `ChipRemove` content is
  never part of the label.
- **M2, a focused chip that unmounts (15.6).** New rule: when a focused chip unmounts for a
  reason other than its own Backspace / Delete (a rolled-back addition, a controlled parent
  dropping the value, a form reset), focus goes to the next chip, else the previous one, else
  the Input. Implemented from the Chip's registration cleanup (which runs before the host node
  is removed) and a Root layout effect that runs after the chips' re-registration, so a chip
  that only re-registered keeps focus.
- **m1, Enter while an open is on its way (15.6, product-owner decision).** With `multiple`,
  Enter with typed text while the listbox is intended open but not committed yet (a slow
  `openChangeAction`, or the keystroke's own open still rendering) is prevented and the text is
  kept: the user typed a search and is about to pick, never "submit this". Judged on committed
  state, so Escape-then-Enter (committed still open until the `toggle` fact) keeps the rules of
  section 8 unchanged.
- **m2, a chip focused while an open is on its way (15.6).** Focus arriving on a chip also
  cancels an open that is requested but not shown, with a close request, so the listbox never
  shows under a focused chip.
- **m3, printable keys on a chip (15.6).** Printable means one code point
  (`[...key].length === 1`, astral characters included) other than Space. Ctrl / Meta are
  checked for the navigation keys only; a character typed with AltGr
  (`getModifierState("AltGraph")`, Ctrl+Alt on Windows) is handed over; an IME start
  (`key === "Process"`, `keyCode` 229) focuses the Input too. Whether the composition then runs
  in the Input is part of the manual pass (no engine automates an IME on a chip here).
- **n1 (15.7).** While `Chips` is empty it carries no name at all: the consumer's `aria-label` /
  `aria-labelledby` are removed with the library's (a role-less `div` may not be named).
- **n2 (types, docs only).** `ComboboxRootProps` is a union, so `Partial<ComboboxRootProps>` is
  not assignable to either member and no longer spreads into `Combobox.Root`; a wrapper types
  its partial props as `Partial<ComboboxSingleProps>` (or the multiple variant). Noted on the
  docs page.
- **n3.** conventions 1.1 had two "A second exception" paragraphs: the Combobox one is now the
  third, after NumberField's. No rule changed.
- **n5 (15.7).** The removal is announced optimistically, in the event; a rejection brings the
  chip back without a second announcement.
- **m4 (docs).** The JSDoc and docs rows of `allowCustomValue` and `defaultInputValue` describe
  the multiple behaviour; the props table's type column shows both variants' types.
- Tests (jsdom, `combobox-multiple.test.tsx`, "review fixes"): one row per finding, plus a
  Combobox row for the #151 rule (a reset equal to the intended value dispatched while changes
  are in flight, the final value the reset target).

## 2026-11-26, #164: Combobox `multiple`, re-review follow-ups

From the follow-up section of `memo/reviewer/review-164.md` (re-review of 33fdcb17). F2 is a
product-owner decision. Sections changed: combobox.md 3.1 (the `openChangeAction` comment),
5.6 (the requests table), 15.6.

- **F1 (implementation only, no rule changed).** The record of a focused chip whose
  registration ended (M2 of the entry above) is good for its own commit only: it is dropped in
  a microtask. A chip cleanup in a commit the Root is not part of (a `label` from state below
  the Root, a boundary inside it toggled from below) left a record behind, and a later Root
  commit that removed that chip pulled focus back into the combobox from wherever it had gone.
  The Root's layout effect runs before microtasks when the Root commits in the same commit, so
  the M2 cases are unchanged. jsdom row "F1".
- **F2 (15.6, 5.6, 3.1).** The cancel of an open still on its way when a chip takes focus (m2 of
  the entry above) was `requestClose` with `reason: "dismiss"`, so `openChangeAction(false)` ran
  with a dismissal reason, against "never called for a dismissal". It is a **request**, as
  Alt+ArrowUp is: `openChangeAction(false, { reason: "activate" })`, `details.event` the
  `focusin`, and `onOpenChange` is not called (nothing was shown). Listed among the requests in
  the 5.6 table, the `openChangeAction` comment of 3.1, the JSDoc of `openChangeAction` and
  `ComboboxOpenChangeDetails.reason`, and the docs row. The jsdom row "m2" asserts the reason

## 2026-11-26, #166: hover-card.md, the HoverCard design (proposed)

Wave 23, part of #162. Written by the architect from
`docs/research/wave23-hovercard-select-multiple.md` part 1; **proposed**, not yet decided by
the user. New document `design/components/hover-card.md`. Working notes:
`memo/architect/hovercard-notes.md`; probe `memo/architect/probes-166/interest-rules.mjs`
(Chromium 156).

What the design takes from the research, and where it differs:

- Taken: a library-mode Popover base with a link Trigger and the Popup right after it;
  `manual` by default, `hint` and `interestfor` behind flags, never `auto`; Tab from the
  Trigger enters the card; no `aria-describedby` and no `aria-expanded`; nothing on touch on
  the JS path; the Trigger is a link or a button that opens nothing on click.
- Different: **focus inside the card does not keep it open against the pointer.** The research
  said "focus inside the card keeps it open". The probe shows Chromium's native rule is "the
  latest event wins" (a hover-opened card whose button was clicked closes when the pointer
  leaves; a focus-opened card closes when the pointer crosses and leaves it), and the design
  follows that on the JS path so the two paths agree and the timer pair stays Tooltip's.
- Different: no `aria-details` from the library (the research offered it as an option). The
  Popup follows the Trigger in the DOM, which is the case in which HTML-AAM drops the relation
  for a `popovertarget` popover.
- Added: one mode only (no JS-free mode; opening is always a request, so content loads on
  interest and Suspense holds the open); every user close is a fact with reason `"dismiss"`;
  a press on the Trigger closes the card and cancels a coming open, on both paths (Chromium's
  native behaviour keeps it open); "no open until fresh interest" after Escape, a Trigger
  press and the library's focus return, enforced at the `beforetoggle` interception on the
  flagged path; `interestfor` written after hydration; every show is a no-focus show; the
  `<span>` Popup for cards inside running text; `role="group"` as the default role; delays of
  600 / 300 ms.

Changed in other documents, in the same commit:

- `popover.md` 2.9: the recommendation to put `interestfor` on the Trigger ("click opens in
  every engine, interest adds hover on Chromium") is withdrawn. HTML's author guidance (added
  to whatwg/html PR #11006 on 2026-11-24) says not to combine interest and activation for the
  same rich target on one element. The rows of 2.9 stay: they describe what a consumer's own
  `interestfor` button does, and HoverCard's flagged path runs on them. No code change follows
  from the edit.
- `tooltip.md` 4.1: the sentence that called a pinned tooltip "a Popover with `commandfor` +
  `interestfor`" now says that pattern is not offered.

Conventions: **no rule changes.** HoverCard applies 3.9 (requests and facts), 3.5, 5.1, 8 and
13 as written. When the component is implemented, the enumerations that name the overlay
components need HoverCard added, without a change of rule: `overlay-open-state.md` 3.9 ("the
four overlay Roots"), 3.9.11 (no JS-free mode), 3.9.13 (the warning's Roots); `conventions.md`
2.2 (the `"activate"` and `"dismiss"` rows: interest and lost interest, which Popover 2.8
already uses), 5.3 (the types `fsui-hover-card`, `-open`, `-close`), 8 (the two flags), 9.1 /
9.2 (the folder and the `./hover-card` export).

Open for the user (the product owner escalates; recommendation first):

1. The name: `HoverCard` (recommended) or `PreviewCard`.
2. Keyboard model: Tab enters the open card (recommended, the platform's model) or the card is
   kept out of the Tab order (Radix).
3. Popover 2.9: withdraw "hover to preview, click to pin" as documented here (recommended),
   and whether `Popover.Trigger` should also warn in development when given `interestfor`.
4. A press on the Trigger closes the card on both paths (recommended) or the card stays as in
   Chromium's native behaviour.
5. Default delays: 600 / 300 ms (recommended) or Tooltip's 250 / 150 ms (Chromium's
   `interest-delay` defaults).
6. Ship `experimental_interestFor` in the first version (recommended by the research) or add
   it after Chromium 160's specification alignment has been re-probed.

Checks for the implementation (not rules; the tests will be the reference):

- Browser rows, all three engines: Tab from the Trigger enters an adjacent card; a `manual`
  `<div popover>` shown `inert` moves no focus even with an `autofocus` descendant; Escape with
  focus inside returns focus to the Trigger and no card re-opens; a press outside with focus
  inside leaves focus where the press landed; the pointer leaving a card that holds focus
  closes it; a card inside a modal Dialog and inside a Menu; a nested card; Escape with a Menu
  open inside the card closes the Menu only.
- Chromium only, flagged: the rows of probe `interest-rules.mjs` through the real component;
  an interest timer running when the Trigger is pressed opens nothing; long-press is not
  testable in Playwright.
- Re-probe on Chromium 160 (`InterestForSpecAlignment`): "suppress next focus interest" may
  make the library's flag redundant for the focus return; the `loseinterest`-without-hide
  behaviour of a re-shown popover (popover.md 2.9) must still hold.
- Safari: the hoisted Popup (hover-card.md 1.1, shape 2) is not after the Trigger in the Tab
  order. Documented degradation, not a library bug.
- jsdom covers the timers, the request / fact routing, pending and the overlap walkthroughs.

## 2026-11-26, #166: HoverCard decided and implemented

The user's decisions on the six open questions of the design entry above (and a seventh), all
as the design recommended:

1. The name is `HoverCard` (`@funstack/ui/hover-card`).
2. Tab from the Trigger enters the open card (the platform's model).
3. Popover 2.9's "hover to preview, click to pin" recommendation is withdrawn as the design
   entry describes; `Popover.Trigger` gets **no** development warning for `interestfor`.
4. A press on the Trigger closes the card and cancels a coming open, on both paths.
5. The default delays are 600 / 300 ms.
6. `experimental_interestFor` ships in the first version; a re-probe on Chromium 160
   (`InterestForSpecAlignment`) is a follow-up (`memo/developer/issue-166.md`).
7. The close of a shown card on lost interest is a fact (`onOpenChange`), not a held request.

`hover-card.md` status: decided. Implemented in `packages/ui/src/hover-card/` (Root, Trigger,
Popup, `use-hover-card-interest.ts`), with jsdom and three-engine browser tests, a docs page
and a playground demo.

Enumerations extended without a change of rule, as the design entry listed:
`overlay-open-state.md` 3.9 (five overlay Roots, `hover-card.md` 2.5 in the per-component
list), 3.9.2 (HoverCard's lost-interest hide, Escape and press outside among the facts the
library triggers; the `openChangeAction` / `"dismiss"` crossover row), 3.9.11 (no JS-free mode),
3.9.13 (five Roots); `conventions.md` Decisions 11 and 2.1 (the `onOpenChange` handlers), 2.2
(the `"activate"` row names interest, the `"dismiss"` row lost interest, the crossover row a
HoverCard's Escape or press while its open is pending), 5.3 (the `fsui-hover-card` types), 8
(both flags); `testing.md` (five overlay Roots); `internal-hooks.md` (the `usePopoverPopup`
options below). Conventions 9.1 and 9.2 enumerate no components, so nothing changed there.

Shared code changed for HoverCard (no behaviour change for the other components):

- `usePopoverPopup` gains three options: `quietShow` (every library show is a no-focus show,
  the refused re-open's `inert` path), `allowOpen` (a predicate on every routed foreign or
  interest open at `beforetoggle`; `false` cancels it and dispatches nothing) and `elements`
  (the tag names of the development element check; HoverCard allows `<span>`).
- `usePopoverPopup` reports a recorded close intent's `event` as recorded, `undefined`
  included, instead of falling back to the `toggle` event (hover-card.md 2.5: the close when
  `disabled` becomes true has no event). Every other popover-like intent records an event, so
  nothing else changes.
- The controlled-without-`onOpenChange` warning calls the popup "card".

Refinements of the design while implementing, edited into `hover-card.md` in the same commit:

- 2.4: one "no open until fresh interest" flag for both paths. The design had a one-shot flag
  around the JS path's focus return; the flag is now set before the hide (a `hint` popover
  restores focus to the Trigger inside `hidePopover()`), read by the JS path's `focus`
  listener, and cleared by the Trigger's `pointerenter` as well as `pointerleave` and `blur`
  (without `pointerenter`, a pointer coming onto the Trigger after an Escape that returned
  focus there could not open the card until it had left once).
- 2.2, the document Escape row: `preventDefault()` only when a shown card closed. An Escape
  that cancels an open nobody can see yet passes through (inside a modal dialog it closes the
  dialog), as Tooltip's "Escape while closed passes through".
- 6.2 "a dismissal can say that it returns no focus to the Trigger" (section 12): implemented
  in HoverCard's own dismissal, not as a hook option. For lost interest and a press outside
  with focus inside the card, the library blurs the focused element before `hidePopover()`,
  so neither the hook's focus-return fallback nor a `hint` popover's own focus restore moves
  focus to the Trigger; focus goes to `<body>`, and a press then puts it where it lands.
  Escape with focus inside focuses the Trigger itself, right after the hide, under the flag.

Not changed, for review: hover-card.md 2.2's paragraph after the table still says "focus inside
the card keeps it open" among the differences from Tooltip, which contradicts Decisions 6 and
2.1 ("the latest event wins", the probe). The implementation follows Decisions 6.

## 2026-11-26, #165: a JS multi-select, `MultiSelect` (proposed)

Design for GitHub issue #165 (part of #162, wave 23). **Proposed**: written by the architect,
not yet accepted and not implemented. User decision so far (2026-11-26, after
`docs/research/wave23-hovercard-select-multiple.md` part 2): build a JS multi-select listbox
now, a select-only combobox on the Combobox `multiple` machinery of #164; the architect
proposes where the API lives. Working notes in `memo/architect/select-multiple-notes.md`.

Sections changed:

- New document `design/components/multi-select.md`. Part A compares the three homes
  (`Select.Root multiple`, an input-less Combobox, a dedicated component) and recommends the
  dedicated `MultiSelect`; A.4 says what changes under each home. Part B is the behaviour,
  written against neutral part names so that it survives the choice of home.
- select.md 13: one sentence that points at the proposal. No rule of Select changes.
- Not edited yet, on purpose: conventions 1.1 (the part vocabulary rows for `Trigger`, `Value`,
  `Option`; the validity element as a use of the NumberField exception), 2.5 (the list of
  set-valued owners) and 5.3 (the transition types). They depend on the home and the name,
  and #164's branch edits the same paragraphs; they are edited when the design is accepted.

The reasoning worth keeping:

- **Why not `Select.Root multiple`.** Select is a real `<select>`; every part is a native
  element (`select`, `option`, `optgroup`, `legend`, `hr`, `selectedcontent`). The JS listbox
  shares no element with it, so the flag would change the element of every part, and the
  parts cannot see the flag in their types. Base UI, React Aria and Ark can offer the flag
  because their single Select is already a JS listbox. The flag would also make "no
  JavaScript, works before hydration" conditional, and it would take the name the native
  multi drop-down needs later (select.md 13), which would force the API to be limited to what
  a native select can do (research option D).
- **Why not an input-less Combobox.** The machinery is shared whatever the home. Sharing the
  namespace gives `Combobox.Trigger` a second meaning that must be known on the server, adds a
  third variant to the Root's props, leaves text-only state fields behind and leaves
  `required` (the Input's) without a home.
- **The name.** `MultiSelect`, not `Listbox`: #162 uses "Listbox" for the inline widget.
  Multiple-only by name; the single select is the native one.
- **The Trigger is `button[role=combobox]`** with DOM focus, `aria-activedescendant` and a
  `popovertarget` written after hydration (the light-dismiss exemption `Combobox.Trigger`
  uses). It renders an explicit `aria-expanded` from `shown`, the one invoker that does:
  the state is required by the role and the button has no `popovertarget` before hydration.
- **A pick toggles and never closes; Tab does not toggle.** The first is #164's rule. The
  second departs from the APG's single select-only combobox, where Tab selects.
- **Order is pick order**, #164's, because options are unmounted while the listbox is closed.
  A native `<select multiple>` posts in document order; recorded as a trade-off.
- **`Value` shows what the consumer renders.** The label cache has nothing for a value whose
  option was never mounted, which is every default value in the server HTML, so the documented
  form is function `children` with the consumer's own names. An `items` prop was not added.
- **`required` needs an element.** A button and a hidden input are barred from constraint
  validation. The proposal is a visually hidden one-option `<select>` after the Trigger whose
  `required` is computed from the optimistic value (conventions 3.6). Unlike NumberField, the
  browser's bubble is the hidden element's own, since no visible element can hold validity.
- **The Label's click focuses and does not open**, as a native label on a `<select>`:
  `<label for>` on a button would forward a click.

Open decisions for the user (recommendation first):

1. Home: a dedicated `MultiSelect` / `Select.Root multiple` / an input-less Combobox.
2. Name, if dedicated: `MultiSelect` / `Listbox`.
3. Showing the selection: a `Value` part with function `children` and no chips / chips.
4. `required`: the hidden validity element / not in v1.
5. Order of the value: pick order / document order.
6. Open-state API: the full overlay API / none (only if the home is `Select.Root multiple`
   and a later swap to the native element is wanted).
7. Scope of v1: no `Clear`, no range selection, no select-all / add some.
8. Single selection in this component: no / yes.

To verify in a browser at implementation: multi-select.md B.16.
## 2026-11-26, #165: `MultiSelect` decided and implemented

The user accepted the eight recommendations of the entry above (issue comment, 2026-11-26):

1. A dedicated component, `MultiSelect` (`@funstack/ui/multi-select`).
2. The name `MultiSelect`.
3. A `Value` part with function `children`, no chips.
4. `required` through a hidden validity `<select>`.
5. The value in pick order.
6. The full open-state API.
7. No `Clear`, no range selection, no select-all in v1.
8. Multiple selection only.

multi-select.md is now "decided": the neutral part names of Part B are the parts of
`MultiSelect` (`Root`, `Label`, `Trigger`, `Value`, `Popup`, `List`, `Option`, `Group`,
`GroupLabel`, `Status`, `Empty`); Part A stays as the reasoning, A.5 records the decisions.

The conventions edits the entry above left for acceptance:

- conventions 1.1: the part vocabulary rows `Root` (one hidden input per value for a set:
  Combobox `multiple`, MultiSelect), `List`, `Trigger` (MultiSelect's is the combobox,
  `button[role=combobox]`), `Label` (a button surface whose forwarded click it turns into
  focus), `Option`, `Empty`, `Status`, `Value` (MultiSelect's `span` with function `children`);
  the validity element as a use of the NumberField exception; MultiSelect's Root under the
  Combobox hidden-input exception.
- conventions 2.5: MultiSelect in the list of set-valued owners.
- conventions 5.3: the MultiSelect row (`fsui-multi-select`, `-open`, `-close`, `-select`,
  `-deselect`).
- Also: conventions 3.2 (the `shown` row: MultiSelect's Trigger renders `aria-expanded`), 3.6
  (a surface that cannot hold validity at all: no mirror, the `invalid` cancelled), 7.4 (the
  "written after hydration" row names MultiSelect's `popovertarget`).

Amendments made at implementation:

- **B.10, B.16: the browser's bubble is not shown.** The B.16 check failed in Firefox: the
  bubble of the hidden element stays after the focus hand-over, over the place where the
  listbox opens, and takes the clicks there (the first options could not be clicked). A probe
  with a plain visible `<select required>` showed Firefox's bubble swallowing the clicks below it
  as well, so it is the platform's; script can neither move nor dismiss it. The fallback of
  `memo/architect/select-multiple-notes.md` is taken: the validity element's `invalid` is
  cancelled, a submission attempt (`:user-invalid`) focuses the Trigger through the Field's
  first-invalid collector, and the message is `Field.Error`'s. Outside a Field a blocked submit
  only moves focus. The validity element is `autocomplete="off"` and disabled with the Trigger;
  the Trigger carries an inline `anchor-name` while `required` is set.
- **field-form.md 4.2, 7.1, 7.2**: `Field.Label` cancels its click and focuses a `<button>`
  control (owned `onClick`, composed); a Field listens for `invalid` on a `validityElement`
  outside a registered element that cannot validate itself; `focusTargetOf` returns a button
  control itself; a MultiSelect row in the 7.2 table and in the `useFieldValueChange` table.
- **B.7, B.1**: `data-placeholder` is on `Value` whenever the selection is empty, also with
  function `children`.
- **select.md 13**: `multiple` on `Select.Root` is dropped (not passed to the `<select>`) as
  well as warned about: a `<select multiple>` under `value={string}` is a broken state.
- **B.15**: the shared files are named as they landed (below).
- `MultiSelectTriggerProps` also omits `onKeyUp` (owned: Space is prevented on `keyup` too).

Implementation notes (not rules):

- The listbox hooks moved from `combobox/` to `internal/` once: `use-option-registry.ts`,
  `use-active-option.ts`, `use-deferred-leave.ts` (flat), `action/use-multiple-selection.ts`
  (generic over the component's extra detail fields), and the new `form/hidden-values.tsx`.
  `use-active-option.ts` gained a resolver form of the pending edge and a `loading` hold, both
  unused by Combobox. Menu's typeahead moved to `internal/typeahead.ts`. Combobox's tests pass
  unchanged; `design/internal-hooks.md` lists the files.
- Tests: the shared value-action suite runs against MultiSelect (driver
  `packages/ui/src/__tests__/drivers/multi-select.tsx`, transition types in
  `packages/ui/src/multi-select/multi-select-transition-types.test.tsx`);
  `packages/ui/src/multi-select/multi-select.test.tsx` (jsdom) and
  `packages/ui/src/multi-select/multi-select.browser.test.tsx` (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit
  through branch CI). Notes in `memo/developer/issue-165.md`.

The points left to verify by the entry above (B.16), as found:

- Chromium's accessibility tree exposes the Trigger as a `combobox` whose `expanded` follows
  the shown listbox with `popovertarget` and the explicit `aria-expanded`. Firefox and WebKit
  have no automated probe.
- The validity element: see the amendment above. `reportValidity()` on it returns `false` (a
  candidate for constraint validation, not "not focusable"); form-state restoration is ruled
  out with `autocomplete="off"`, not probed across a reload.
- A `<label for>` press held 150 ms on an open listbox: light dismiss, then focus on the
  Trigger, no re-open (all three engines).
- WebKit: focus is on the Trigger after a mouse press.
- Still manual: the screen-reader pass (the toggle under `aria-activedescendant`, the
  Trigger's text as the value); WebKit's `flip-block` nested in a Popover (302008).
## 2026-11-26, #165: `MultiSelect`, review amendments

From the review of the implementation (`memo/reviewer/review-165.md` on `review/165`).
Sections changed: multi-select.md B.3, B.10; the docs page's Trigger row.

- **B.10: the submission attempt is reported once.** Inside a Field with a `Field.Error`, the
  Field's capture listener on the validity element cancels the `invalid` and reports the
  Trigger to the first-invalid collector; the Trigger's own listener reported it again, which
  the collector took for a new attempt: focus left document order (a MultiSelect below an
  invalid text field took focus) and the browser's message was announced on top of the
  `Field.Error` description. The Trigger now reports only when the event was not cancelled
  already.
- **B.10: the validity element is not anchored.** With the bubble cancelled nothing points
  at its box, so it is a plain visually hidden element, and the Trigger no longer gets an
  inline `anchor-name` (which overrode a consumer's).
- **B.3: the Trigger carries the Root's `form`** (owned; `form` is omitted from
  `MultiSelectTriggerProps`), so the reset listener follows the right form when there is
  neither `name` nor `required`.
- **`onKeyUp` is no longer owned.** Probed: with the `keydown` of Space prevented, no engine
  activates the button on `keyup` (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit through branch CI), so the guard
  went; `onKeyUp` passes through (it was never in B.3's `Omit`).

Implementation notes (not rules):

- A key or a hover while the List is loading disarms the pending edge, so the user's choice is
  not replaced when the options arrive. The `loading` hold of `use-active-option.ts` is now a
  function read in the layout effect (the Status's ref count): render state missed a Status
  that registered in the open commit itself.
- `use-multiple-selection.ts` casts the component's extra fields, not the whole details.
## 2026-11-26, #167: `AlertDialog`, the design (proposed)

Architect, for the product owner and the user; part of #162 (wave 24). New document:
`design/components/alert-dialog.md`. Not implemented. Also touched, without a rule change:
`design/overlay-open-state.md` 3.9 (one sentence: `AlertDialog.Root` is `Dialog.Root` with
`modal` fixed) and dialog.md 3.3 (the `role` pass-through points to AlertDialog). Notes:
`memo/architect/alert-dialog-notes.md`.

What the document proposes:

- A separate namespace `AlertDialog` at `@funstack/ui/alert-dialog` (`Root`, `Trigger`,
  `Popup`, `Title`, `Description`, `Cancel`, `Action`, `Form`), every part running the code of
  a Dialog part with props fixed. Chosen over a preset prop on `Dialog.Root` because the
  preset would have to reach two other parts and would leave `modal={false}` and
  `lightDismiss` on the types of a component that must reject them.
- Fixed: modal, `role="alertdialog"` (owned), no light dismiss (no `closedby` attribute is
  needed: a modal dialog's default is `closerequest` in every engine).
- Escape closes, as a fact. The APG's alert dialog pattern has no keyboard section and points
  to Dialog (Modal); Radix closes on Escape as well. `closedby="none"` was not taken: Chromium
  and Firefox only, cannot be emulated in Safari (the anti-abuse rule), and it does not stop
  `requestClose()`.
- Initial focus on the first enabled Cancel through Dialog's `autofocus` mechanism; in JS-free
  mode the Cancel renders `autoFocus` so the server HTML has it.
- `Action` is `Dialog.Close` with an `action` (own transition, `whilePending` default
  `"ignore"`, close on resolve, open on rejection), except that with `action` it renders no
  native close command: a click before hydration must not close the dialog as if the work had
  been done.
- The confirm without JavaScript is `AlertDialog.Form action={serverFunction}`.
- Requests and facts are Dialog's, unchanged. No conventions rule changes.

Open decisions for the user (recommendation first):

1. **Separate namespace** (recommended) or a preset on Dialog.
2. **Escape closes** (recommended), or an opt-in that renders `closedby="none"` and works in
   two engines of three.
3. **An Action with `action` is no native close invoker** (recommended), or the same markup as
   `Dialog.Close`. If accepted: whether `Dialog.Close` and `Popover.Close` with an `action`
   should follow (a separate issue; it changes shipped behaviour before hydration).
4. **`AlertDialog.Form` in the namespace** (recommended), or `Dialog.Form` used inside an
   AlertDialog and documented.
5. **The Cancel stays active while an Action is pending** (recommended; the consumer disables
   it with their own optimistic state), or the library ignores the Cancel and renders
   `aria-disabled` on it while any Action of the Root is pending.
6. **Dialog's transition types and data attributes** (recommended: one stylesheet for both),
   or `fsui-alert-dialog*` types of its own.
7. **A development warning for a missing Description** (recommended), or none, as Dialog.

Not verified; to check at implementation:

- React's `autoFocus` on a Cancel that mounts while a JS-free alert dialog is already open
  calls `.focus()` and takes focus; the design accepts it (the content of a JS-free dialog is
  mounted with the page). If it turns out to bite, the fallback is the Popup's mount effect
  alone, with focus before hydration left to the platform's first-focusable rule.
- A disabled Cancel carrying `autofocus` is skipped by the dialog focusing steps in the three
  engines (the rule says "first enabled Cancel"; in JS-free mode the attribute is rendered on
  each Cancel).
- Base UI's AlertDialog is not in the design's section 4 table: its docs page (read
  2026-11-26) lists `escape-key` and `outside-press` as change reasons but does not state the
  defaults. The APG and Radix rows were read the same day; "Radix does not close on a click
  outside" is from its source as remembered, not from the docs page.
- Screen readers announce title and description with the role on open (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver).

Gap recorded, not solved here: an action-prop confirm that fails cannot show an inline error
next to live buttons without an Error Boundary, because an action that catches its error
resolves and a resolved action closes the dialog. The Form shape with `Form.Root` covers it.
A "resolve but stay open" signal on Close parts would be a conventions question (actions
return nothing today).
